fact_check_summary: Re-read late on 13 Nov 2026: 38 signal pages plus 14 archived signal IDs, 43 Market product pages (incl. the Popular top 30), 15 Code Base pages and 5 source files, 3 blogs, all 88 ranking pages (re-fetched and re-parsed independently), FP Markets, AMF, CFTC, RePEc/AAII, Gulf Times, GitHub, and the lab files cited. 79 claims: 59 OK, 14 WRONG, 6 UNVERIFIABLE. The conclusion stands and is if anything too kind: nothing near +50 %/month, no robot worth buying. Corrections that change what the trader reads: (1) long-lived accounts (6-11 years) make a median +1.7 %/month, not +2 to +5 %; (2) 'live drops are 3-5x the backtest' is a cherry-picked overstatement: Gold Reaper's own seller announces up to 30 % in backtest, the live default account fell 46 %, the V2 account 17 %; (3) the Popular top 30 has 23-25 robots under 6 months, not 21; (4) the 4,205 signals are MQL5's ranking, not all public signals (MQL5 says 8,000+, and wrecks like Waka Waka are not ranked), so the base rates flatter; (5) Quantum Queen sold for 599-1,299 USD (Queen X 1,199.99), not 999-1,999; (6) Emperor's page does not say 'not a grid' and its worst MQL5 drop is 40.5 %; (7) Scalp IC Markets ECN's author does not say 'same broker', and that signal (and Soma) trip the synthesis's own alarms; (8) only one EA Happy signal trades in 6 seconds. Every credible-robot figure (Gold Trade Pro, Gold Reaper, Range Breakout, Soma, Scalp IC Markets) matched its live page; real-account status, ages, drops and deposit loads confirmed. Myfxbook not checked (the lead reported HTTP 403).

Réponse courte : non pour acheter ou copier un robot MQL5. Oui, un peu, pour apprendre et pour tester 2 idées. Rien de ce qu'on a trouvé ne mène à +50 % par mois.
Ce qu'on a lu le 13 novembre 2026 : 46 robots du Market MQL5, les 4 205 signaux du classement public MQL5 (tous sur comptes réels), 27 robots gratuits (Code Base, GitHub), et des études de régulateurs et d'universitaires. Rien acheté, rien installé.
Attention : MQL5 annonce plus de 8 000 signaux, et son classement n'affiche pas tout. Des comptes ruinés, comme celui de Waka Waka, n'y figurent pas. Les chiffres ci-dessous sont donc plutôt trop flatteurs.
Seul juge : le résultat réel vérifié, c'est-à-dire un signal MQL5 sur compte réel d'au moins 12 mois. Les backtests, les captures d'écran et les promesses ne comptent pas.
Sur 1 429 signaux réels de 12 mois ou plus, aucun ne fait +50 % par mois. 17 (1 %) font +20 % ou plus, 119 (8 %) +10 % ou plus. Le signal typique fait +2,6 % par mois, avec une chute de 41 % en route.
Sur 2 ans ou plus, le meilleur fait +24 % par mois, mais il a perdu 53 % à un moment.
Les meilleurs robots honnêtes du Market (un stop sur chaque trade, pas de grille) font +3,7 à +6,9 % par mois sur 2 à 3 ans : Gold Trade Pro, Gold Reaper, Range Breakout. Tous ont connu des chutes de 17 à 46 %. Et pour chacun, MQL5 note que 80 % du gain est venu en 11 à 30 jours seulement.
Les comptes qui durent gagnent peu. Sur les 50 comptes du classement qui ont 6 à 11 ans d'historique, la moitié fait moins de +1,7 % par mois. Les 5 meilleurs font +4 à +5,7 % par mois, avec des chutes de 19 à 78 %.
Notre robot : son mois typique est au mieux d'environ +12 % sur le papier, à 5 % de mise. Même à la moitié du papier, il serait au niveau des meilleurs robots honnêtes.
Aucun robot crédible ne le bat. Aucun ne le complète de façon prouvée : les bons robots or font les mêmes cassures que nos règles. En acheter un ajouterait du risque et coûterait de 250 à 3 200 $.
Les pièges :
- Les grilles et martingales : de petits gains presque tous les mois, puis le compte vidé en une nuit. Quantum Queen, ancien best-seller, a été retiré en 2026 ; selon un concurrent, son signal montrait une chute de 85 % avant de disparaître. Waka Waka est à -95 % après 8 ans, et il est toujours vendu 2 800 $ avec la promesse « +12 000 % ».
- Le classement « Popular » est du marketing : 23 à 25 des 30 premiers ont moins de 6 mois, et 3 seulement ont 12 mois de réel.
- L'historique importé : un compte peut publier son passé après coup. Après la publication, la croissance est en général divisée par deux, ou plus.
- Les vitrines : signaux à 999 $ par mois sans aucun abonné, trades de quelques secondes impossibles à copier, comptes de 60 à 300 $.
- Les backtests : le réel fait souvent pire. Gold Reaper : le vendeur annonce lui-même « jusqu'à 30 % » de chute en backtest avec ses réglages par défaut ; son compte réel aux réglages par défaut a chuté de 46 %.
- La durée : sur 882 signaux mis en avant par MQL5 entre 2014 et 2021, 3 seulement tradent encore.
Le contexte : chez FP Markets (Europe), 74,51 % des comptes particuliers perdent de l'argent sur les CFD. Dans une étude universitaire, copier les meilleurs d'un classement a fait perdre de 79 à 92 %.
+50 % par mois, c'est ×130 en un an. Le meilleur fonds du monde (Medallion) fait environ +4 % par mois avant frais. L'AMF a mis en garde contre des robots frauduleux qui promettaient 5 à 15 % par mois.
Même en théorie, une méthode de la qualité de la nôtre plafonne vers +13 à +18 % par mois, avant les écarts du réel. Monter la mise ne mène pas à +50 % : les comptes réels à +20 % par mois ont subi une chute médiane de 53 %.
Ce qu'on peut en tirer : 2 idées nouvelles pour notre labo, à tester avec la même méthode (règle écrite avant, test sur 2013-2021, un seul regard sur 2022-2025) : 1) acheter l'or juste après sa réouverture de 18 h, heure de New York ; 2) jouer le retour au calme des paires de devises pendant la nuit (c'est notre hypothèse : les vendeurs de robots de nuit ne publient pas leurs règles).
Elles serviraient à diversifier, pas à multiplier les gains. Nos propres données font déjà douter de la première. Et le meilleur compte de nuit déclenche une de nos alarmes : ses capitaux ont chuté de 38 % quand le solde ne baissait que de 23 %, et sa charge de compte monte à 35 %.
L'idée du meilleur robot de cassure à plusieurs marchés (Range Breakout) a déjà été testée chez nous sur le Nasdaq, le Dow, le DAX, le yen, le bitcoin et l'ether : échec. Elle ne tient que sur l'or, où notre robot l'utilise déjà.
Et une liste d'alarmes pour juger n'importe quel robot : pas de stop, mise qui grossit après une perte, plusieurs positions dans le même sens, capitaux très en dessous du solde, moins de 12 mois de réel, promesse de plus de 10 % par mois.

Demo, contest and cent accounts are deleted automatically (https://www.mql5.com/en/signals/rules). So every signal figure below is real money. The 'Started' date on some pages is later, because it is when the signal was registered. Growth per month is our own compound calculation from total growth and weeks. Myfxbook pages returned HTTP 403 to our fetch tool, so no Myfxbook 'track record verified / trading privileges verified' status could be checked. None of the top-30 pages links Myfxbook anyway. Review counts differ between the list and the product page (for example Quantum Emperor shows 506 on the list and 591 on the page). We use the product-page figure. result.base_rates: WHAT COUNTS: a real-account MQL5 signal of the same product with at least 52 weeks of history. MQL5 rules allow signals only from real accounts. Myfxbook could not be checked (HTTP 403), and no top-30 page links Myfxbook. SAMPLE 1, top 30 of the MT5 'Popular' list on 13 Nov 2026: 3 of 30 (10%) qualify. They are The Gold Reaper (145 and 107 weeks), Range Breakout EA (104 weeks) and Quantum King (64 weeks, grid + martingale). At least 21 of the 30 were first published after 30 May 2026, going by the dates on their pages. Only 4 are older than 12 months. 2 link no signal at all (Scalping Robot Pro, AI Golden Life). 1 links a disabled signal (EA Super Trend XAUUSD). The other 24 show signals under 37 weeks old, most of them a few weeks. SAMPLE 2, the 10 most-reviewed paid EAs on the first two Popular pages (83 to 865 reviews): 3 of 10 qualify (Quantum Emperor at 62 weeks, Quantum King, Gold Reaper). The most-reviewed, EA Gold Stuff (865 reviews, on sale since 2020), has no live signal left. The three MQL TOOLS bestsellers (122-176 reviews, $1,099-$2,499) never linked any third-party record. The former bestseller Quantum Queen (more than 400 ratings) is withdrawn, and its signal was deleted after an 85% drawdown. ALL 46 PRODUCTS CHECKED: we found 7 records of 12 months or more. 3 are stop-loss breakout robots still alive: Gold Trade Pro (162 weeks, about 5.9% a month compounded, worst balance drawdown 32%), Gold Reaper (145 weeks, about 3.7% a month, worst 45.6%) and Range Breakout (104 weeks, about 6.9% a month, worst 28%, profit factor 1.18, 80% of the gain made on 11 days). 2 are grid or recovery robots still alive: Quantum King (about 11.9% a month) and Quantum Emperor (about 8.5% a month). Both have equity drawdowns near 30%, and money moved in and out many times the start balance. 2 are grid robots that crashed: Waka Waka (-95% after 440 weeks) and Quantum Queen (signal deleted). Long records from the same sellers outside the top lists are modest: Night Hunter Pro +194% in 316 weeks (about 1.5% a month), PAI +349% in 380 weeks (about 1.7% a month), Profalgo's Bitcoin Reaper Live -12% after 72 weeks, ORB Master +27% in 59 weeks with a 50% drawdown. No record of 12 months or more averages above about 12% a month, and none is anywhere near +50% a month (x130 in a year). Every record showing 30-80% a month is 26 weeks old or less. These sit on $60-$300 accounts (MoonDog, Gold Beaver, My AI Gold) or rest on one huge trade (TitanForge). LIVE vs BACKTEST: wherever both exist, live is clearly worse. Gold Reaper backtests show a max drawdown of 8-12% and a profit factor near 2.7. The default-settings live account reached a 45.6% drawdown with profit factor 1.6, and a cited Myfxbook account 41.7% and 1.08. TitanForge's backtest shows 97% winners and a profit factor of 49.7. Live, its equity fell 30% within 31 trades. Quantum Queen X won 1,589 of 1,590 baskets in backtest, and the single loss was 104% of the account. Then the same kind of loss happened live. A seller's study of 43 paid gold EAs, on default inputs with costs not stated, found 19% blew up even in the tester (https://www.mql5.com/en/blogs/post/773167). Most product pages give no backtest numbers in text at all. Note: the 'Sharpe ratio' field on MQL5 signal pages (0.05-0.21 here) is per trade and cannot be compared with our weekly Sharpe of about 2.0. Only one seller signal we saw had real copiers (Gold Reaper V2, 52 subscribers). Most are priced $599-$1,000 a month with 0 subscribers: they are showcases.
result.conclusions: (1) No: the MQL5 bestsellers cannot give the client +50% a month. No verified real-money record of a year or more comes close. The best surviving stop-loss robots made about 3.7-6.9% a month compounded over 2-3 years: Gold Reaper, Gold Trade Pro and Range Breakout. Along the way they went through 28-46% drawdowns. Two grid or recovery robots show 8-12% a month over 14-15 months, but they run the same mechanics that just wiped out Quantum Queen and Waka Waka. (2) Our robot's 'typical month at best +12% on paper at a 5% stake' is already above every record of a year or more that we found. Buying a bestseller would not raise the ceiling. It would add risk and cost $250-$3,200. (3) The Popular rank reflects launches and marketing, not results. At least 21 of the top 30 are under 6 months old, and one was 6 days old at number 3. 'Only X copies left' and rolling price deadlines appear on most pages. At least one seller admits trading free products for reviews, and reviewers say the same of two others. Seller signals priced at $999 a month with 0 subscribers are showcases, not proof. (4) The smooth-curve-then-crash pattern is current, not historical. Quantum Queen was withdrawn in July 2026. Its successor Quantum Queen X was withdrawn after reported losses of 94-96% in one night (6 Oct 2026), and its '30 months, +5,000%' signal was deleted. Waka Waka's 8-year record has just fallen to -95% while the robot is still sold at $2,800. EA Gold Stuff (865 reviews) has no live record left. At least 6 seller signals we tried now return 404 or are disabled. (5) A red-flag checklist that caught nearly every bad case: no stop loss, or a stop loss off by default. Words like 'recovery', 'additional orders', 'lot multiplier' or 'Lots Step'. Winners above 90% while losses are bigger than wins. Equity drawdown far above balance drawdown (Vortex Gold 34.9% vs 16.6%, TitanForge 30% vs 0.4%). Deposit load above 20% (Waka Waka 185%). Accounts of $60-$300. Deposits and withdrawals larger than the account. A signal younger than the product, or older signals deleted. The MQL5 warning 'Share of days for 80% of growth is too low'. (6) What we can take is a few rule ideas, all with stop losses and single positions, and mostly close to what we already run. Daily support/resistance breakouts on gold D1 (Gold Trade Pro). Asian range to London-open breakout on gold, DAX and US30 (Range Breakout EA; also Aura Gold Pro's 'London Open Momentum'). Opening-range and volatility-contraction breakouts (Ultimate Breakout System), with the caveat that the seller's own live ORB is +27% with a 50% drawdown. Previous-day momentum with one BTC trade a day (Bitcoin Scalping MT5). A blackout on new trades 60-90 minutes around high-impact news (MQL TOOLS). The only reason to test them is to find a low-correlation sleeve. Expect overlap with ORX, Brk72 and D4H. (7) Indices and crypto: index-focused bestsellers are rare. The only one with a long live record (Range Breakout) has a thin edge (profit factor 1.18), and the one Nasdaq preset found (Institutional SMC) has no live record at all. Crypto bestsellers have records of 5-39 weeks, or none. The longest crypto records from a serious seller are flat to negative (Bitcoin Reaper -12% after 72 weeks), or +91% in 160 weeks with a 71% drawdown. (8) If the client still wants to buy something, set a minimum bar. At least 12 months of real MQL5 signal on at least $1,000, with no large deposits or withdrawals. Max deposit load under 15%. Equity drawdown close to balance drawdown. Real subscribers. Then plan for a live drawdown 2-4 times the backtest, and for 2-6% a month at best. The FP Markets account we found (Aura Gold Pro: +585% in 43 weeks, 35% drawdown, -13% this month) shows how quickly a hot record can turn.

result.base_rates:
All numbers measured by me on 2026-11-13 from mql5.com (list pages https://www.mql5.com/en/signals/mt5/list?orderby=weeks and https://www.mql5.com/en/signals/mt4/list?orderby=weeks, all pages). Average monthly gain = headline growth compounded over the account's weeks.

1) TODAY'S RANKING: 4,205 real-account signals (2,680 MT5 + 1,525 MT4).
- 12 months or more of history: 1,429 signals. Average +10%/month or better: 119 (8.3%). +20%/month or better: 17 (1.2%). +30%/month or better: 2 (0.1%). +50%/month: 0. The typical (median) one makes +2.6%/month with a 41% max drawdown; 14% are below zero overall.
- 24 months or more: 685 signals. +10%/month or better: 19 (2.8%). +20%/month: 1 (0.1%, MSC SuperGold Pro, 53% drawdown). +30% or +50%: 0. Median +2.3%/month, median max drawdown 46%; 12% below zero.
- The winners' drawdowns: the 119 signals at +10%/month or better (12m+) have a median max drawdown of 48%. 48% of them fell 50% or more at some point and 23% fell 70% or more. The 17 at +20%/month or better: median drawdown 53%, and 9 of 17 fell 50%+. Only 37 of 1,429 (2.6%) combine +10%/month with a drawdown of 30% or less. Over 24+ months only 7 of 685 (1.0%) do. Of those 7: two are the same declared AUDCAD/NZDCAD grid (Harmonizer, published Oct 2026 and Feb 2026); three are one vendor's 999 USD/month showcase accounts with 2-6 minute trades and 0 subscribers (Happy Signal, EA Happy News Eightcap, EA Happy Gold Eightcap); one was published 4 days ago (Aurum Titan, 2399030). Only Soma PureGold Indexes and Oil (2268766) is a normal record, public from day one.
- Nearest to +50%/month: EA Happy Gold BB High Risk (2392590), about +45-49%/month over 15-16 months. It is a 999 USD/month vendor showcase with 6-second trades and 0 subscribers, published 51 days ago, and MQL5 itself warns 'High risk of negative slippage when copying deals'. Samurai AI OG (2378358) shows +38.6%/month but made it before publication; since publication (5 months) +4.7%/month.
- For scale: +50%/month for 12 months is x130 (1,000 EUR to 130,000 EUR); +20%/month is x8.9; +10%/month is x3.1.

2) THE PUBLICATION EFFECT. MQL5 imports an account's whole past when a signal is created (rules, section III.5), so headline growth mixes old history with live months. Among the 17 detailed signals with at least 6 months before and 6 after publication, 15 grew more slowly after publication: median +10.2%/month before vs +5.1%/month after (mean 14.3% vs 5.9%). Examples: Happy Signal 22.6% -> 5.1%, HJM1 25.8% -> 8.3%, Multi EA Trading 33.4% -> 3.8%, Deux ex machina 9.6% -> 1.5%, NoPain 7.3% -> 2.5%. Of the 11 detailed signals public from day one with 12+ live months, the best did 21.1%/month (Kenni Trades, 19 months, now decaying) and the rest 6-15%/month.

3) EARLIER YEARS (archived copies of the MQL5 showcase on Arquivo.pt: 60 snapshots, Nov 2014 to Oct 2021, listing 882 different signals; each checked on mql5.com today). Today 878 of the 882 (99.5%) return 'trading signal not found', 1 is 'disabled by the provider' and only 3 (0.3%) still trade. By growth shown at the time: 1,000%+: 99 signals, 98 deleted, 1 disabled, 0 alive. 300-999%: 162, 3 alive (1.9%). 100-299%: 249, all gone. Under 100%: 372, all gone. All 31 signals that had 100+ subscribers are gone, including AlterProfit MT5 (875 subscribers, +4,466% in 2021), CALM (843 subscribers, +2,505%, 44% drawdown, June 2017), AD AUDUSD (469, +2,573%), Arimbi (456), Moustache (438), Blackwave Pacific (417, +6,509%), Bushmills (279, +3,693%) and Night Healer (265, +7,610%). All 20 signals of the June 2017 'Top MetaTrader 4 / 5' lists are gone. Where the archive kept a full page, the stars were grids or averaging systems. Bushmills (June 2020) had 97% winners but an average loss 7.7x the average win and called itself a 'smart grid'. Hydrogen (July 2021, +3,318% in 28 weeks, 50 subscribers) had an 80% max deposit load on NZDCAD/AUDCAD/gold. Jack Flash Slow Real (July 2021) declared an 'Averaging Martingale Technique' with a 144% deposit load; KapKap had 112%. Caveat: a deleted page cannot be inspected, so I cannot tell how many were wiped out and how many were just closed. The deletion rate is the same for low-growth signals, so the clear lesson is that almost no signal lasts 5+ years, whatever its growth. The 3 survivors are slow: Blackwave California (192529) +2.3%/month since 2016 with a 61% max drawdown; RFactor Portfolio JM (743742) +3.5%/month; R Factor Mean Reversal (734515) +4.5%/month.

4) SISTER ACCOUNTS. The 27 author pages behind today's strongest signals list 207 signals (only those not deleted). 20 of them (10%) are wrecked (drawdown 70%+ or growth -50% or worse) and 53 (26%) have a drawdown of 50%+. Examples: NoPain's author has 'UpHill MT5 Old' (1245170) at -74% with a 99% drawdown. The R Factor author has 'R Factor Broker Papperstone' (973932) at -59% with a 97% drawdown, while his 'R Factor Broker FPMarkets' (973927) is at +230%. The EA Happy vendor has 'EA Happy Gold GridNews' (1714611) with an 89% drawdown. 'Chicken dinner' (2299696) is at -63% (drawdown 99%) and 'Gold Scalp Test' (2380747) at -98%. Deleted accounts do not show, so the true share is higher.

5) WHO COPIES TODAY. All 4,205 ranked signals together have only 748 subscribers (about 4.8M USD copied). The most-copied MT5 signal (Combo Profile 2026) has 69 subscribers and only 45 weeks of history; 31% of all subscribers sit in signals younger than 12 months. In 2017-2021 single signals had 400-875 subscribers (AlterProfit MT5 875, CALM 843, AD AUDUSD 469, Arimbi 456, Moustache 438, Blackwave Pacific 417). Every one of them has been deleted.

6) INDEPENDENT CHECK. Dorfleitner et al. (2018, Quarterly Review of Economics and Finance 70:160-171) studied social-trading platforms. Following the traders with the highest past returns 'leads to high losses'; follower numbers and invested capital do not predict returns; no selection strategy beats costs (https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/quaeco/v70y2018icp160-171.html).
result.conclusions:
SHORT ANSWER: no. MQL5 Signals cannot give him +50% a month.

1. Nobody does it on a real account. Today's ranking has 1,429 real-account signals with 12+ months of history. None averages +50% a month; only 17 (1.2%) average +20% and 119 (8.3%) +10%. Over 24+ months the best is +24% a month (one signal, 53% drawdown), and only 19 of 685 (2.8%) reach +10%. A typical signal makes about +2.5% a month with a 40-45% max drawdown.

2. Headline growth is inflated by history published after the fact. MQL5 imports an account's whole past when the signal is created, and providers publish after a hot streak. In 15 of the 17 signals I could split, growth slowed after publication: median +10% a month before, +5% after. Several of today's 'stars' went public days or weeks ago (Gold Trend Following: 4 days; Harmonizer: 36 days; EA Happy Gold BB: 51 days).

3. The stars do not last. I re-checked 882 signals that MQL5 showcased between 2014 and 2021 (archived copies on Arquivo.pt). Only 3 still trade today (0.3%); 878 no longer exist. None of the 99 that showed 1,000%+ growth survives. None of the 31 that had 100+ subscribers survives either (one had 875 in 2021). The 3 survivors grow 2-5% a month. Deleted pages cannot be inspected, so blow-ups and quiet closures cannot be told apart. But where the archive kept details, the stars were grids or averaging systems (Bushmills: 97% winners with an average loss 7.7x the average win; Hydrogen, Jack Flash and KapKap: deposit loads of 80-144%).

4. The fast growers are mostly the wrong kind:
- Grid and averaging robots on AUDCAD, NZDCAD or gold. They show a smooth curve, then a crash: equity drawdowns of 50-90% and deposit loads of 80-140%.
- Vendor showcases priced 999 USD/month with 0 subscribers. Their trades last seconds or minutes, so a copier cannot get the same price.
- Accounts that hold losing trades, with equity far below balance.
Sister accounts of the same providers include wrecks: 10% of the 207 signals on their author pages are at -50% or worse, or have a 70%+ drawdown.

5. Copying costs extra. A signal costs 30-50 USD a month. Slippage adds to it: MQL5 itself flags 'Too frequent deals may negatively impact copying results' on several of these signals and 'High risk of negative slippage when copying deals' on one. The broker matters too. One author runs the same R Factor robots at several brokers. - A checklist he can apply to any signal or robot:
  1. Read 'Started' and count only the months after it.
  2. Equity drawdown much larger than balance drawdown = losing trades kept open.
  3. Max deposit load above 30% = too much exposure.
  4. 80%+ winners with an average loss 2x+ the average win = averaging or grid.
  5. One pair like AUDCAD, NZDCAD or AUDNZD = classic grid.
  6. Deposits and withdrawals larger than the balance = the growth % can mislead.
  7. Price 999 USD and 0 subscribers = a sales showcase.

result.conclusions:
Short answer: the free, open-source MQL5 world will not give +50% a month. We read 27 robots. Not one has a VERIFIED LIVE record: no MQL5 real-account Signal, no Myfxbook. The authors of the best ones publish no signals at all. Every number we found is a backtest. Even the backtests are modest when they are honest. Gold Breakout H4: about +10% a year at 1% risk, flat in 2020-2023 (https://www.mql5.com/en/code/77691). SessionReopenEA: about +3.3% a year (https://www.mql5.com/en/code/77060). London Breakout: +3.2% in 2025 (https://www.mql5.com/en/code/78293). NY Open Candle: +25.6% in 2025 at 1% risk, 91 trades (https://www.mql5.com/en/code/78392). The best of these is about +2% a month in a backtest. To reach +50% a month you would need roughly 25 times the risk, and the 7-11% drawdowns at 1% risk would then wipe the account out. Our robot (weekly Sharpe about 2.0, at best about +12% a month on paper at a 5% stake) is already well ahead of anything free we found.

Popularity is a trap. The most downloaded free gold robots are a grid that doubles its lot with no stop (XANDER Grid, 6,362 downloads), a grid that can close every position on the account (Pending tread, 6,522), and an EA with no results and a bug in its sell signal (KA-Gold, 7,255). The only 'BTC robot' in the MT5 Code Base (CryptoTrend, 2,321 downloads) contains no trading code, just a panel and a Bybit link. 'Quantum XAUUSD' uses a random number in its signal. GOLD_ORB, the 331-star GitHub gold ORB, never sends a real order with its default settings because of a missing-brace bug. Do not run any of these.

What we can take: a few small, new, cheap-to-test ideas. They would add diversification, not multiply returns. Test each through the lab's normal steps (in-sample, attacks, then one look at 2022-2025). In order of evidence: (1) Gold daily reopen drift: buy within 10 minutes of 18:00 New York, Monday to Thursday evenings New York, hold 2 hours, stop 2 x the mean H1 range. This has the best evidence: 11 years, t = 3.4 to 4.1 after real costs. But it is tiny (+1.6 to 1.9 bps a trade) and very sensitive to the spread. (2) US100 'Monday dip': buy at Tuesday's open after a down Monday that closed in its bottom quarter (IBS 0.25 or less), exit at Wednesday's close (https://www.mql5.com/en/code/78343). (3) US100 RSI(2) pullback in an uptrend on daily bars: buy when RSI(2) is below 5-10 and price is above SMA200, exit on a close above SMA5. This is the classic Connors version, not the Code Base code. (4) US100 calm-afternoon long: entries from 10:00 to 14:00 New York after a recent NR7 bar when short-term volatility is below 1.6 x long-term, flat at 16:00. It is ported from the GER40 and JPN225 EAs, which were mined from thousands of candidates, so test it strictly out of sample (https://www.mql5.com/en/code/78380). (5) An NR4/NR7 'quiet day' filter added to our gold Asian-range breakout (https://www.mql5.com/en/code/78259), plus the bare prior-day high/low stop breakout on gold as a control (https://www.mql5.com/en/code/77900).

What confirms our choices: two independent authors found the same gold edges we trade. A 20-bar H4 Donchian breakout on gold (PF 1.77, flat 2020-2023, +24% and +27% in 2024-2025 at 1% risk) matches our Donchian 4-hour rule. Asian/London breakouts make small gains (+3.2% in 2025 at 0.5% risk). Opening-range EAs on US100 match our Nasdaq opening-range rule. Nothing public matches our gold Friday-afternoon rule, our Nasdaq noise-band rule, our crypto 72-hour breakout or our bitcoin-follows-Nasdaq rule. Those remain our own.

result.scope: Independent evidence on retail trading robots, signals and copy trading. Covered: (1) regulator loss statistics: EU/ESMA, France/AMF, Australia/ASIC, and FP Markets' own mandatory EU disclosure; (2) peer-reviewed studies of real retail FX traders and of social/copy trading; (3) studies that compare backtests with later live results; (4) why grid, martingale and averaging strategies show smooth curves, with documented gap events that break them; (5) platform rules (MQL5 Signals, Myfxbook verification); (6) regulator fraud cases and warnings about trading robots. Read-only web research done on 13 Nov 2026. Nothing was bought, downloaded to run, or logged into. Extracted PDF texts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-gold-orb/340d9f5a-4d28-5733-90cb-10a10699d00b/scratchpad/mql5_survey/indep_dl/. Limits: (a) I found no peer-reviewed study of MQL5 Signals or Myfxbook survival. The closest rigorous evidence is from other social-trading platforms and from broker data on retail FX. (b) The Myfxbook help page, Forex Peace Army and some SSRN pages block automated reading, so their wording comes from search-index snippets. (c) I found no independent, fully documented case study of one named MQL5 or Myfxbook grid EA blowing up with complete live data. What exists is forum anecdotes, one seller's backtest study, and market-wide gap events. Each item below says what kind of evidence it is.

items.kind: Regulator data (EU)
items.live_evidence: VERIFIED LIVE, at scale. EU national regulators analysed real retail CFD accounts at many brokers. These are not backtests.
items.numbers: 74-89% of retail CFD accounts typically lose money. Average loss per client: EUR 1,600 to EUR 29,000 (press release, 27 Mar 2018). Leverage caps from 30:1 down to 2:1 depending on the asset. Brokers must close out an account's positions at 50% of required margin. Negative balance protection. Each broker must publish its own loss share, recomputed every 3 months over the past 12 months. An account counts as losing if its realised plus unrealised CFD profit over those 12 months is negative (renewal decision: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dec/2018/1636/oj/eng).
items.red_flags: Losing money is the normal outcome for retail CFD traders, with or without a robot. The 50% margin close-out is how grid and martingale accounts die in a fast move: positions are closed automatically at the worst point.
items.claimed_strategy: Not a strategy. This is the base rate for all retail CFD trading, manual or automated.
items.markets: All retail CFDs: FX, gold, indices, crypto.
items.testable_idea: Apply ESMA's own test to our robot. For each rolling 12-month window in 2022-2025, would the account count as a 'losing account'? Report the share of losing windows, not only the average.

items.name: FP Markets' own EU loss disclosure (First Prudential Markets Ltd, CySEC)
items.kind: Broker disclosure, required by EU rules
items.live_evidence: VERIFIED LIVE. This is the broker's own figure for its real retail accounts, computed by the ESMA method.
items.numbers: 74.51% of retail investor accounts lose money when trading CFDs with this provider (read on 13 Nov 2026). The entity is First Prudential Markets Ltd, CySEC licence 371/18.
items.red_flags: About 3 in 4 of the trader's fellow clients at his own broker lose money over 12 months. Clients who use robots and copy trading are included in that count.
items.claimed_strategy: Not a strategy. Base rate at the trader's own broker (if he is on the EU entity).
items.markets: All CFDs offered by FP Markets EU.
items.testable_idea: Treat 74.51% as the starting assumption. Any robot we consider must show live evidence strong enough to overcome a 3-in-4 chance of losing.

items.name: AMF study of French retail forex and CFD clients, 2009-2012 (Observatoire de l'epargne letter no. 10, Oct 2014)
items.kind: Regulator study (France)
items.live_evidence: VERIFIED LIVE. Data from regulated brokers on 14,799 active French retail clients over 4 years.
items.numbers: 89% lost money over the 4 years. Average loss about EUR 10,887; median loss EUR 1,843. The 13,224 losers lost about EUR 175 million in total. The 1,575 winners gained EUR 13.8 million in total, about 13 times less. On a one-year view, 75-89% lost depending on broker and year (about 84% overall). More trading meant bigger losses. Clients with 250+ orders (52% of clients) lost EUR 18,741 on average. Clients with 1,000+ orders (23%) lost EUR 31,349 on average. No learning: clients active in all 4 years went from 82% losing (average EUR 4,989) in year one to about 88% losing (average EUR 26,745) over 4 years. The same letter cites US CFTC data (60.5% of US retail forex clients lost money in Q2 2014) and the Polish regulator (82% lost over 2011).
items.red_flags: The AMF notes that ads push placing 'many orders, sometimes automatically' with maximum leverage. In the data, the clients who traded most lost most. A high-frequency robot fits that losing profile.
items.claimed_strategy: Not a strategy. Base rate for French retail forex and CFD clients.
items.markets: Forex, CFDs on all underlyings, binary options.
items.testable_idea: Measure our robot's trade count and its real cost per trade on the live account. In the AMF data, losses grow with the number of orders.

items.name: ASIC product intervention notice on CFDs (Oct 2020), plus ASIC REP 828 (FY2024 data)
items.kind: Regulator data (Australia, FP Markets' home regulator)
items.live_evidence: VERIFIED LIVE. Data from up to 61 licensed CFD issuers on real retail accounts.
items.numbers: 2017 review: over 12 months, 63% of clients lost money on margin FX and 72% on other CFDs. 16 Mar to 19 Apr 2020 (13 issuers with over 85% market share): 56.9-63.2% of accounts lost money each week. Net retail losses were A$774,238,833 in five weeks. More than 1.1 million positions were closed out at the liquidation level. More than 15,000 accounts went negative, by A$10.9 million in total. In 2018: 9.3 million positions were closed out automatically, and over 41,000 accounts (5.7%) ended with negative equity (A$33 million). An FCA test cited in the notice: at 500:1 leverage with a 50% close-out, a client who adds no money over two hours is closed out on the losing side 81% of the time, and loses all the margin or more 44% of the time. Caps in force since 29 Mar 2021: 20:1 for gold and major indices, 2:1 for crypto, 30:1 for major FX. FY2024: 68% of retail CFD investors lost money, more than A$458 million in total including A$73 million in fees (https://asic.gov.au/about-asic/news-centre/find-a-media-release/2026-releases/26-004mr-asic-secures-nearly-40-million-in-refunds-to-investors-and-drives-change-after-cfd-sector-falls-short/).
items.red_flags: In volatile weeks, leverage and margin close-outs destroy accounts. Grid and martingale robots run close to full margin, so they are closed out first.
items.claimed_strategy: Not a strategy. Base rate and margin close-out data.
items.markets: FX, indices, gold, commodities, crypto CFDs.
items.testable_idea: Replay our robot through 16 Mar to 19 Apr 2020 with a 50% margin close-out and the 20:1 and 2:1 caps. Report the worst equity point, not only the final result.

items.name: Heimer and Simsek, 'Should retail investors' leverage be limited?' (Journal of Financial Economics, 2019)
items.kind: Academic, peer-reviewed
items.live_evidence: VERIFIED LIVE. Three data sets of real US retail forex accounts, before and after the 2010 CFTC leverage cap (50:1 on major pairs, 20:1 on minor pairs).
items.numbers: The cap cut trading volume by 23%. It reduced high-leverage traders' losses by 40%. It reduced brokers' operating capital by 25% (SSRN abstract). ASIC summarises the result as a gain of 18% per month in high-leverage traders' portfolio returns (ASIC notice, paragraph 32).
items.red_flags: More leverage made retail traders lose more, not win more. A +50% a month target needs very high leverage.
items.claimed_strategy: Not a strategy. Causal evidence on leverage.
items.testable_idea: Run our robot at 1x, 2x and 3x the planned stake on 2022-2025. Report the median and the worst 12-month outcome at each stake. Expect the median to stop improving well before the 'paper' maximum.

items.name: Hayley and Marsh, 'What do retail FX traders learn?' (Journal of International Money and Finance, 2016)
items.kind: Academic, peer-reviewed
items.live_evidence: VERIFIED LIVE. Daily activity of over 95,000 retail FX traders on one leading platform over 30 months.
items.numbers: The median trader loses $5.56 per active day. More than 5% of traders lost money on every day they traded. Even the 99th-percentile trader's average daily profit is only 'tens of dollars'. A trader with 100 days of experience is only 5.8% less likely to have a winning month than a novice. Performance gets slightly worse with experience, and even very experienced traders keep losing money. Traders trade smaller or quit after a losing day.
items.red_flags: Because traders quit after losses, the ones still visible are survivors. Public signal lists go through the same filter.
items.claimed_strategy: Not a strategy. Base rate and learning evidence.
items.testable_idea: When reading any list of MQL5 signals, assume the dead accounts are missing. Ask how many signals the provider has closed or deleted.

items.name: Chague, De-Losso and Giovannetti, 'Day Trading for a Living?' (Brazil)
items.kind: Academic working paper, complete market data
items.live_evidence: VERIFIED LIVE. Every individual who began day trading Brazilian equity index futures in 2013-2015 (exchange data).
items.numbers: 19,646 people started, and 1,551 (7.9%) kept going for more than 300 sessions (CXO summary: https://www.cxoadvisory.com/investing-expertise/day-trading-a-bust/). Of those who lasted at least 300 days, 97% lost money. Only 0.4% earned more than a bank teller (US$54 a day). The best trader earned US$310 a day, with a daily standard deviation of US$2,560. No evidence of learning.
items.red_flags: Even the persistent minority nearly all lose. The few winners are small and very volatile, and they are the ones that get advertised.
items.claimed_strategy: Not a strategy. Base rate for persistent retail day traders.
items.testable_idea: Treat a 1-in-100 survivor as luck unless its edge is explained and checked on data it was not built on.

items.name: Dorfleitner et al., 'To follow or not to follow' (Quarterly Review of Economics and Finance, 2018)
items.kind: Academic, peer-reviewed (social and copy trading)
items.live_evidence: Real track records of signal providers on Ayondo and Wikifolio, 2013-2016. The following strategies are simulated on those live records.
items.numbers: Following the providers with the highest accumulated returns, rebalanced monthly, lost 92% over 36 months on Ayondo and about 79% over 29 months on Wikifolio. Choosing by risk-adjusted measures cut the losses to 36% and 13% (AAII summary: https://www.aaii.com/journal/article/returns-for-social-trading-platforms-are-negative). No following strategy earned a positive abnormal return after costs (Carhart four-factor model). Very active trading predicts lower returns. Follower counts and invested capital do not predict returns.
items.red_flags: Picking the top of the leaderboard by return is the worst way to choose. Subscriber count is not a sign of quality. Very active providers do worse.
items.claimed_strategy: Copying top-ranked signal providers.
items.markets: Equities, FX and CFDs on German social-trading platforms.
items.testable_idea: If we ever screen MQL5 signals, rank them by risk (drawdown, Sharpe, equity versus balance), never by growth %. Also check that the provider trades rarely enough that costs do not eat the edge.

items.name: Apesteguia, Oechssler and Weidenholzer, 'Copy Trading' (Management Science, 2020), with Heimer and Simon on myForexBook
items.kind: Academic, peer-reviewed experiment, plus a working paper on a social network of FX traders
items.live_evidence: Laboratory experiment, not market data. Supporting evidence comes from real trading records linked to social posts on myForexBook (abstract only).
items.numbers: Showing traders how others performed significantly raised their risk taking. Adding the option to copy raised it further. The authors conclude that copy trading leads to excessive risk taking (abstract: https://econ-papers.upf.edu/en/onepaper.php?id=1615). On myForexBook, posts were biased towards positive returns, even though the network revealed a low success rate among retail traders (Cleveland Fed WP 15-22: https://www.clevelandfed.org/publications/working-paper/wp-1522-facebook-finance-social-interaction-investing).
items.red_flags: Leaderboards reward the riskiest providers. Screenshots and posts over-report wins.
items.claimed_strategy: Copy trading in general.
items.testable_idea: Expect the 'best performers' people copy to be the most leveraged. Check risk before return.

items.name: IOSCO Final Report FR/06/2025 on online imitative (copy, mirror, social) trading, May 2025
items.kind: International regulator report
items.live_evidence: Survey of member regulators plus complaint data. Not a performance study.
items.numbers: One respondent said copy trading is most common in FX, CFDs and crypto. In an Ontario OSC experiment, people offered the option to copy a 'high performing' user made 18% more trades than a control group. Italy's Consob reports 2020-2023 complaints: one client said the copied strategies were always loss-making, and clients of unauthorised copy services often reported trades placed without their instructions and the loss of nearly all their capital. IOSCO lists leaderboards and rankings that may mislead investors as a supervisory issue: about lead traders' expertise, risk-adjusted and past returns, and the incentives lead traders receive.
items.red_flags: Lead traders may be paid in ways that conflict with followers' interests. Leaderboards can mislead.
items.claimed_strategy: Copy trading in general.
items.testable_idea: When the trader browses MQL5 Signals, read the subscription price and subscriber ranking as a reason for providers to take risk in order to show high growth.

items.name: Wiecki, Campbell, Lent and Stauth, 'All that glitters is not gold' (Quantopian, 2016)
items.kind: Academic working paper
items.live_evidence: Backtests compared with at least 6 months of true out-of-sample results, for 888 algorithms.
items.numbers: Backtest Sharpe ratio explains less than 2.5% of the differences in out-of-sample Sharpe (R squared below 0.025). The more backtests a developer ran, the bigger the gap. Machine learning on many backtest features reached only R squared = 0.17 (abstract: https://quantopian-archive.netlify.app/forum/threads/q-paper-all-that-glitters-is-not-gold-comparing-backtest-and-out-of-sample-performance-on-a-large-cohort-of-trading-algorithms).
items.red_flags: A beautiful backtest says almost nothing about the future. Heavily optimised EAs show the biggest gap.
items.claimed_strategy: Systematic US equity algorithms.
items.testable_idea: Judge MQL5 products only on forward live results after their publication date. For our own rules, keep the one-look validation discipline.

items.name: Suhonen, Lennkh and Perez, 'Quantifying backtest overfitting in alternative beta strategies' (Journal of Portfolio Management, 2017)
items.kind: Academic, peer-reviewed
items.live_evidence: Backtest period compared with the live period of bank strategy indices (live index values, not client accounts).
items.numbers: 215 strategies from 15 banks. Median Sharpe 1.20 in backtest versus 0.31 live, a 73% fall. 65 of 215 had a negative live Sharpe. Only 18 of 215 matched or beat their backtest. The most complex strategies fell about 30 percentage points more than the simplest.
items.red_flags: Even professionally built strategies sold by banks lose most of their backtest Sharpe. Retail EAs with more settings should be expected to lose more.
items.claimed_strategy: Bank 'alternative beta' indices across asset classes.
items.testable_idea: Cut our robot's Sharpe of 2.0 by 50-75%, to 0.5-1.0, and check what monthly return remains at our stake. Set the trader's expectations on that figure, not on paper results.

items.name: Bailey, Borwein, Lopez de Prado and Zhu, 'Pseudo-mathematics and financial charlatanism' (Notices of the AMS, May 2014)
items.kind: Academic, peer-reviewed
items.live_evidence: Mathematical result with simulations. No live data.
items.numbers: With only 5 years of data, try no more than 45 independent model configurations. Otherwise you are almost guaranteed to find a strategy with an in-sample annualised Sharpe of 1 but an expected out-of-sample Sharpe of zero. Without the number of trials, the risk of overfitting cannot be assessed (summary: https://sciencedaily.com/releases/2014/04/140410103005.htm).
items.red_flags: EA sellers never say how many variants or settings they tried. Offering 'optimised' set files is a symptom of this.
items.claimed_strategy: Any backtested strategy.
items.testable_idea: Count every rule variant our lab tried while building the 10 rules. Compute the minimum backtest length (or a deflated Sharpe) and show it next to the Sharpe of 2.0.

items.name: Lo, 'Risk management for hedge funds' (Financial Analysts Journal, Nov/Dec 2001): 'Capital Decimation Partners'
items.kind: Academic, peer-reviewed. Shows how smooth curves hide crash risk.
items.live_evidence: A hypothetical strategy run on real January 1992 to December 1999 prices, as an illustration.
items.numbers: The strategy sold S&P 500 puts about 7% out of the money each month. Result: 3.7% average per month, Sharpe 1.94 (S&P 500: 0.98), only 6 losing months out of 96 (S&P 500: 36), total return 2,721% (S&P 500: 367%). A second fund buys more as the price falls and sells as it rises; Lo shows this copies a short put. In his words, 'returns are positive most of the time, and losses are infrequent, but when they occur, they are extreme.'
items.red_flags: Grid, martingale and averaging EAs have the same profile: high win rate, smooth curve, almost no losing months, then one catastrophic loss. A high Sharpe from such a curve is not evidence of skill.
items.claimed_strategy: Selling crash insurance; adding to losing positions.
items.markets: US equity index options and stocks (the logic applies to any grid on gold, indices or crypto).
items.testable_idea: For any EA, count its losing months. If there are almost none and the method adds to losing positions, treat it as a short-put profile and stress test a 10% one-day gap.

items.name: Documented gap events that wipe out averaging and grid positions: Swiss franc 2015, March-April 2020, gold on 30 Jan 2026
items.kind: Market events: broker statements, regulator data, news
items.live_evidence: VERIFIED LIVE: real broker losses and real prices.
items.numbers: 15 Jan 2015: the Swiss National Bank removed the EUR/CHF floor. FXCM said client accounts owed it about $225 million in negative balances. Alpari UK went into insolvency (https://www.financemagnates.com/forex/brokers/alpari-uk-first-major-casualty-chf-lcg-group-facing-2-5-mln-losses/). March-April 2020: more than 1.1 million Australian retail CFD positions were closed out in five weeks (ASIC notice, item 4). 30 Jan 2026: spot gold fell 9.5% to $4,883.62, the day after a record of $5,594.82; February futures fell 11.4% (https://www.gulf-times.com/article/719640/business/gold-prices-post-biggest-one-day-drop-in-four-decades). Reuters said gold was on course for its biggest daily loss since 1983 (https://gvwire.com/2026/01/30/gold-set-for-steepest-daily-drop-since-1983-silver-eyes-worst-day-ever/).
items.red_flags: A gold EA that buys dips in a grid would have kept adding positions through a 9-11% fall in one session. EUR/CHF range strategies that bought near the floor were destroyed in minutes. Stop orders can be skipped in a gap.
items.claimed_strategy: Range, grid and averaging strategies in general.
items.testable_idea: Stress every candidate EA, and our own robot, with a gold day like 30 Jan 2026, the March 2020 weeks for US100 and bitcoin, and a weekend gap. Require survival with a 50% margin close-out.

items.name: MQL5 Signals rules (MetaQuotes)
items.kind: Platform rules
items.live_evidence: Rules, not results.
items.numbers: III.12: signals can only come from real accounts. III.13: demo, contest and cent accounts are not allowed and are removed automatically. III.3 and IV.2: accounts with leverage above 1:500 cannot be subscribed to. III.7: copying an existing signal is banned. V.10: fraud or falsified past results means the provider's account is blocked and subscribers are refunded. I.16 and VI.1-2: no guarantee of profitability and no responsibility for losses. I.14: the subscriber takes full responsibility for copying.
items.red_flags: 'Real account' does not mean 'good strategy': the rules check the account type, not the risk. The platform disclaims all results. An 'MQL5 signal' shown elsewhere as a screenshot is not verified.
items.claimed_strategy: Not applicable.
items.testable_idea: Count as live evidence only signal pages read directly on mql5.com. Check account type, age, equity versus balance, and max deposit load.

items.name: What 'verified' means on Myfxbook, known ways around it, and the 'incubation' trick
items.kind: Platform help page, watchdog forum, academic analogy
items.live_evidence: Myfxbook (wording from the search index; the page blocks automated reading): 'Track Record verified' means the history shown matches the broker's history. It needs the account number, investor password, broker and server. 'Trading Privileges verified' means the person posting controls the account (checked with a pending order). Neither badge proves skill, that this is the vendor's only account, or that results will continue.
items.numbers: Forex Peace Army describes fake Myfxbook pages (edited screenshots, private or hidden data) and user reports of vendors who trade dozens of accounts and publish the survivor. One thread alleges a vendor advertised demo results at several brokers as real-money results (https://www.forexpeacearmy.com/forex-books/205/fake-myfxbook-accounts-scam). These are allegations, not findings. Academic analogy: mutual funds run privately ('incubated') beat other funds by 3.5% a year risk-adjusted, and the edge disappears once they open to the public (Evans 2010, Journal of Finance: https://ideas.repec.org/a/bla/jfinan/v65y2010i4p1581-1611.html).
items.red_flags: Track Record verified without Trading Privileges; private settings; demo label; cent account; account younger than 12 months; vendor runs many accounts; account stopped updating.
items.claimed_strategy: Not applicable.
items.testable_idea: Ask any vendor for every account ever linked to the product. Require both green badges, a real-money label, more than 12 months of history and recent updates.

items.name: CFTC on trading robots and 'AI bots': 2024 advisory and cases from 2016 to 2024
items.kind: Regulator enforcement and investor advisory (US)
items.live_evidence: Court orders and regulator complaints. Each case says whether it is a finding or an allegation.
items.numbers: Mirror Trading International claimed to trade forex with a 'bot'. It took at least 29,421 BTC (over $1.7 billion) from at least 23,000 US individuals and promised at least 10% a month (advisory). In April 2023 a court ordered $1.73 billion in restitution plus an equal penalty; the CFTC calls it the largest Bitcoin fraud it has charged (https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/8696-23). Parker and Baggett (2016 complaint, allegations): 'never had a losing month', '300% annual returns', a robot with a '+90% success rate', and 'documented and verifiable results' of 11-68% a month in 2014. The CFTC alleged all of it was false and the robot was never tested with real money; 289 customers paid over $853,000 (https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/7469-16). Silver Star FX: automated forex software sold for $199, then $145 a month. It claimed $250-600 a month from a $300 deposit and a 'proven track record', but its creator never used it live. Ordered to pay over $15.6 million in 2021 (https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/8179-20; https://www.financemagnates.com/forex/cftc-fines-silver-star-fx-and-trading-bot-creator-with-15-6-million/). ROFX claimed a 'highly successful automated trading robot' with guaranteed loss coverage; it took $58 million from more than 1,100 customers (https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/8486-22). A 2024 default judgment found misappropriation of over $57 million (https://cftc.gov/node/251031).
items.red_flags: 'Never a losing month'; win rates near 100%; promised returns of 10% or more a month; 'verifiable' results that were simulated; a seller who never trades the robot live; deposits accepted only in crypto.
items.claimed_strategy: Automated forex and crypto trading robots and AI bots.
items.testable_idea: Add these CFTC red flags to our screening sheet. Reject any EA whose seller cannot show a live real-money account that they trade themselves.

items.name: AMF warning on fraudulent trading-robot offers (France, 2 March 2023)
items.kind: Regulator warning (France)
items.live_evidence: Regulator warning based on complaints and supervision.
items.numbers: The offers promised '5% to 15% per month' and 'up to 400% per year' from an 'automatic trading robot'. Investors paid a monthly or yearly licence costing hundreds to thousands of euros. They had to open an account with a 'partner' broker not authorised in France, deposit and withdraw only in crypto, and were pushed to recruit others for commissions, as in multi-level marketing.
items.red_flags: The trader's +50% a month target is 3 to 10 times the monthly returns that the French regulator lists as typical scam promises.
items.claimed_strategy: Automated forex trading robots sold by licence.
items.testable_idea: Before any purchase, check the AMF blacklists and confirm the broker is authorised for France.

items.name: MQL5 seller's backtest of 43 paid gold EAs ('1 in 5 blew up'), weak evidence
items.kind: Seller blog: backtest study (weak evidence)
items.live_evidence: BACKTEST ONLY. Free demos with default inputs, January 2015 to July 2026, M15 chart, '1 minute OHLC' model, $10,000 deposit, 1:500 leverage. The author sells EAs on MQL5.
items.numbers: 43 paid gold EAs costing $50 to $1,999 (median $299). 19% of the EAs that could be measured blew up the account (equity drawdown 60-102%). The $1,999 EA had a profit factor of 0.23 and a 99% drawdown. Median price was $299 for the 'excellent' group and $499 for the blown-up group. Review counts predicted nothing. Every blown-up EA showed strong recent months, while its deep drawdown sat earlier in its history. On grid EAs, balance drawdown understated the true equity risk about 4 times.
items.red_flags: MetaTrader's own help calls '1 Minute OHLC' testing 'faster but less realistic' (https://www.metatrader5.com/en/terminal/help/algotrading/tick_generation). The author has a commercial interest. The findings still match the wider pattern: price and reviews are not signs of quality, and sales pages show recent months only.
items.claimed_strategy: Mixed gold EAs, including grid and averaging types.
items.testable_idea: For any MQL5 Market gold EA, ask for equity drawdown (not balance drawdown) over 2015-2026 on real ticks, covering the 2020 and January 2026 shocks.

result.conclusions:
Short answer for the trader: the independent evidence says robots and signals do not escape the base rate, and +50% a month is not a realistic target.

1) The base rate is losing. At his own broker (FP Markets EU), 74.51% of retail CFD accounts lose money over 12 months. Across the EU the range is 74-89%. In France, 89% of clients lost over 4 years, and the most active lost most. Peer-reviewed studies of 95,000 retail FX traders and of every new Brazilian day trader find that almost all lose and do not learn. In the only rigorous platform study we found, copying the best-ranked signal providers lost 79-92%.

2) Backtests are weak evidence. Live Sharpe ratios fell 73% from backtest (215 bank strategies). Backtest Sharpe explained less than 2.5% of later results (888 algorithms). With 5 years of data, 45 tries are enough to find a Sharpe-1 strategy by luck. US rules force anyone showing simulated results to say they are 'designed with the benefit of hindsight' and that 'no representation is being made that any account will or is likely to achieve' them (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/17/4.41).

3) A smooth curve is a warning, not a comfort. Simply selling crash insurance gave a Sharpe of 1.94 and only 6 losing months in 8 years (Lo 2001). Grid, martingale and averaging EAs have the same shape. Real gap events break them: EUR/CHF in January 2015 (FXCM clients owed it about $225 million), March 2020 (1.1 million Australian retail positions closed out in five weeks), and gold down 9.5% on 30 January 2026. The broker's 50% margin close-out then sells at the worst moment.

4) Fraud is common and well documented. Regulators treat promises of 5-15% a month (AMF) and a 'guaranteed 10% a month' (Mirror Trading International, $1.7 billion) as scam markers. +50% a month is above all of them. Sellers have faked 'verifiable' results, sold robots never run live, and shown demo results as real. 'Verified' on Myfxbook only proves the history matches the broker. It does not prove the seller did not run 20 accounts and show the survivor.

5) The arithmetic. +50% a month is 130 times the money in a year. The best fund on record, Renaissance's Medallion, averaged about 66% a year before fees, about 4.3% a month. Kelly growth theory sets optimal growth at about half the Sharpe ratio squared per year (https://www.efmaefm.org/0EFMAMEETINGS/EFMA%20ANNUAL%20MEETINGS/2011-Braga/papers/0103.pdf). Our own calculation from that formula: with a true annual Sharpe of 2 (our robot), the theoretical ceiling is about +18% a month at full Kelly and about +13% at half Kelly, before any live haircut. Reaching +50% a month would need a true Sharpe above 3.1 at full Kelly, with very deep drawdowns. Our robot's 'about +12% a month at best on paper' is already close to that ceiling. More leverage cannot fix this; the only honest route up is more independent edges, which raise the Sharpe. An EA that shows +50% a month with a smooth curve is almost certainly hiding tail risk (grid or martingale), cherry-picked, or fake.

6) What we can take from the MQL5 world: a rejection checklist and a few cheap tests, not a +50% robot. Reject an EA or signal if it has any of these: no stop loss; lot size grows after losses; many open positions in the same direction; equity far below balance; high max deposit load; almost no losing months; win rate near 100%; account younger than 12 months; demo or cent account; only Track Record verified (no Trading Privileges); results shown only as screenshots or as '1 minute OHLC' backtests; a seller who never trades it live; promises above 5-10% a month. For our own robot: apply the ESMA 12-month losing-account test to rolling windows; haircut the Sharpe by 50-75%; count all variants tried and compute the minimum backtest length; replay March-April 2020 and 30 January 2026 with a 50% margin close-out.

What would change this view: an EA with 2-3 years or more of live real-account MQL5 history, stop losses, equity close to balance, low deposit load and a believable risk-adjusted return. Even then the expected gain is single-digit percent a month, not 50%.

- EU, 2018: 74-89% of retail CFD accounts lose money; average loss EUR 1,600-29,000 per client (https://www.esma.europa.eu/node/84933).
- France, 2009-2012: 89% lost over 4 years; average loss EUR 10,887, median EUR 1,843; losers lost EUR 175 million against EUR 13.8 million won; about 84% lose in any one year. Also cited there: US 60.5% losing in Q2 2014, Poland 82% losing in 2011 (AMF letter no. 10).
- Australia: 63% (margin FX) and 72% (other CFDs) lost over 12 months in the 2017 review; A$774 million net retail loss in five weeks of March-April 2020; FY2024: 68% lost, more than A$458 million including A$73 million in fees (ASIC notice and 26-004MR).

Retail traders over time (peer-reviewed or complete market data):
- Over 95,000 retail FX traders: the median trader loses $5.56 per active day, and experience does not help (Hayley and Marsh 2016).
- Brazilian day traders who lasted 300+ days: 97% lost money and 0.4% earned more than a bank teller (Chague et al.).
- Leverage: the 2010 US cap cut high-leverage traders' losses by 40% (Heimer and Simsek 2019).

Copy and social trading:
- Following the top accumulated-return providers lost 92% over 36 months (Ayondo) and 79% over 29 months (Wikifolio). No following strategy earned a positive alpha after costs (Dorfleitner et al. 2018).

Backtest versus live:
- Median Sharpe fell from 1.20 to 0.31 live (-73%) across 215 bank strategies; 65 of 215 were negative live (Suhonen et al. 2017).
- Backtest Sharpe explained less than 2.5% of out-of-sample Sharpe across 888 algorithms (Wiecki et al. 2016).
- 5 years of data and 45 tries are enough to produce a Sharpe-1 strategy that is pure luck (Bailey et al. 2014).
- 19% of 43 paid MQL5 gold EAs blew up in one seller's default-settings backtest (weak evidence).

Return anchors:
- Medallion, the best-known fund: 66.1% a year gross and 39.2% net on average over 1988-2018, about 4.3% a month gross (https://www.cxoadvisory.com/investing-expertise/proof-of-superior-investment-expertise/).
- Regulators' scam markers: 5-15% a month (AMF 2023); 'at least 10% a month' (Mirror Trading International); 'never a losing month' and 11-68% a month 'verifiable' results (CFTC 7469-16).
- The trader's target of +50% a month equals x129.7 in 12 months and x16,834 in 24 months.
- Kelly ceiling for a true Sharpe of 2: about +18% a month at full Kelly, about +13% at half Kelly. +50% a month needs a true Sharpe of at least 3.1 at full Kelly. The formula is from the EFMA paper; the monthly figures are our own arithmetic.
